phase_boots.coaching_tip: Use Phase active both offensively for chasing and defensively for escaping. Short cooldown means you should spam it whenever moving across the map.

power_treads.coaching_tip: Switch to Int before casting spells to save mana, then switch to Str when taking damage for survivability. Tread-switching is a core efficiency skill.

arcane_boots.coaching_tip: Pop Arcane Boots before teamfights to top off your team's mana. Coordinate with teammates so multiple Arcane Boots aren't used at the same time.

tranquil_boots.coaching_tip: Attacking a hero or being attacked breaks the regen for 13 seconds. Best on roaming supports who need sustain between ganks without returning to base.

travel_boots.coaching_tip: Core item for split-pushing and global map pressure. Use it to join fights across the map and then TP back to push a side lane while the enemy regroups.

guardian_greaves.coaching_tip: The self-dispel on activation is extremely valuable, and Mend restores 325 health and 200 mana to nearby allies -- use it before your team gets too low. The stronger regeneration below 25% health only applies to the wearer, not to the team.

black_king_bar.coaching_tip: Duration shrinks with the first uses (9s, 8s, then 7s), so save BKB for the most critical teamfight moments. Do not waste it on small skirmishes. Activate it when committing to a fight, not preemptively.

glimmer_cape.coaching_tip: Can be cast on allies -- use it to save teammates being focused. The barrier absorbs magic damage even if the enemy has detection, so it still has value in those situations.

ghost.coaching_tip: Excellent against physical burst heroes like PA, Ursa, or Troll. However, beware of magic nukers -- you take 30% more magic damage in ghost form, which can get you killed faster. Don't use it against heavy magic lineups.

force_staff.coaching_tip: Use it to save allies, escape over cliffs/terrain, or push enemies into unfavorable positions. Can be used on enemies to push them away from their team or into yours.

cyclone.coaching_tip: Self-cast dispels silences, slows, and many debuffs. On enemies, use it to set up skillshots (e.g., Lina stun, Leshrac split) or to disable someone while you reposition.

sphere.coaching_tip: Best against heroes with single-target initiation like Beastmaster Roar, Legion Commander Duel, or Doom. Transfer it to your carry if they are the primary target.

lotus_orb.coaching_tip: Apply to your core hero before a fight for the dispel plus spell reflect combo. The dispel alone removes debuffs like silences and slows, and the reflect deters enemies from casting on the target.

aeon_disk.coaching_tip: Essential for squishy heroes who get burst down instantly. The long cooldown means you only get one chance per fight, so be aware of the timer. Best on supports or initiators who need to survive initial burst.

pipe.coaching_tip: Activate before teamfights when facing heavy magical AoE damage (e.g., Zeus, Tinker, Leshrac). The shield absorbs a flat amount, so using it early before the damage comes is ideal.

mekansm.coaching_tip: Use it mid-fight when your team starts taking damage, not when they are already critically low. The burst heal can swing a teamfight. Build into Guardian Greaves when possible.

crimson_guard.coaching_tip: Extremely effective against lineups with lots of physical right-click damage or summon/illusion heroes. Activate it at the start of a teamfight for maximum team-wide benefit.

heavens_halberd.coaching_tip: Use the disarm on the enemy carry right as they commit to a fight: 3.5 seconds without attacks shuts down their physical damage. One of the best items against right-clickers; the armor and evasion also help you stand in front of them.

spirit_vessel.coaching_tip: Must-buy against high-sustain heroes like Alchemist, Huskar, Morphling, and Wraith King. The healing reduction is critical. Also useful on allies for sustained healing.

desolator.coaching_tip: Great for pushing towers since the armor reduction applies to buildings. Core physical damage item for mid-game timing pushes. Works well with other physical damage dealers on your team.

greater_crit.coaching_tip: Pure damage amplifier -- best when you already have sufficient attack speed and base damage. Get attack speed items first, then add Daedalus to multiply your DPS in the late game.

monkey_king_bar.coaching_tip: Essential against evasion heroes like Phantom Assassin, Windranger, or anyone who buys Butterfly or Halberd. Without it, you can miss a huge portion of your attacks.

butterfly.coaching_tip: Powerful late-game item for agi carries, but hard-countered by MKB. Buy it when enemies don't have MKB yet and consider selling it late if they all have True Strike.

assault.coaching_tip: A team-wide physical damage amplifier. The aura benefits your entire team's right-click damage. Best when your team has multiple physical damage dealers.

skadi.coaching_tip: Exceptional late-game item for its stats and the healing reduction on attacks. The slow and heal-cut stack with Spirit Vessel for maximum anti-heal. Great on any right-click hero in the late game.

heart.coaching_tip: Health regeneration of 1% of your max health plus 1.5% of the health you are missing: it heals fastest when you are low, and it does not need you to leave the fight. Best on tanky strength heroes who can absorb sustained damage.

satanic.coaching_tip: Activate Satanic when you're at low HP for a massive heal-through-damage swing. Combine with BKB so you can attack freely during the 6s window without being disabled.

nullifier.coaching_tip: Counters save items like Ghost Scepter, Glimmer Cape, Force Staff, and Aeon Disk by continuously removing their buffs. Essential for carries against enemies who rely on defensive items.

bloodthorn.coaching_tip: Best against mobile heroes like Storm Spirit, Anti-Mage, Puck, or Ember Spirit. Every hero attack on the silenced target deals 50 bonus damage and 60% of the damage it takes during the silence is dealt again at the end, so call the target for your whole team; only your own attacks get True Strike. Upgrade from Orchid when you need more burst.

rapier.coaching_tip: Only buy when you're losing and need a comeback or when you're far ahead and can end the game. If you die with it, the enemy gets it. Best on heroes with built-in survivability or AoE to utilize the damage.

mjollnir.coaching_tip: Excellent against illusion and summon-heavy lineups since the chain lightning proc hits multiple units. Place the Static Charge shield on your frontline hero who will be attacked the most.

radiance.coaching_tip: Rush this item as fast as possible -- its value decreases the longer the game goes. Best on illusion heroes whose illusions carry the burn aura, maximizing map-wide damage.

diffusal_blade.coaching_tip: Devastating against low-mana-pool heroes like Wraith King, Medusa, and CK. The active slow is excellent for chasing down kills. Illusions do not burn mana, so the burn only comes from your hero's own attacks.

silver_edge.coaching_tip: The Break effect is crucial against passive-dependent heroes like Bristleback, PA, Spectre, Huskar, and Viper. Plan your initiation around the Break timing.

blink.coaching_tip: Core initiation item for nearly every hero. It is disabled by player damage, so it is not a reliable escape tool in combat. Initiate with Blink before the enemy can damage you.

invis_sword.coaching_tip: Good for initiation and escape, but countered by Sentry Wards, Dust, and Gem. Do not rely on it as your only escape. Upgrade to Silver Edge later for the Break effect.

ultimate_scepter.coaching_tip: Check your hero's Aghanim's upgrade before buying -- some are game-changing, others are marginal. Prioritize it when the upgrade fundamentally changes how your hero plays.

aghanims_shard.coaching_tip: Extremely cost-efficient mid-game power spike at 1400 gold. Almost every hero benefits from their Shard upgrade. Buy it at 15 minutes if you have the gold -- it is one of the best value items in the game.

refresher.coaching_tip: Best on heroes with high-impact, long-cooldown ultimates like Enigma, Tidehunter, Warlock, Magnus, and Invoker. Double BKB is also extremely valuable in late game.

sheepstick.coaching_tip: The strongest single-target disable item in the game. Use it before the enemy pops BKB. Chain it with other disables for a guaranteed kill. Late-game must-have for intelligence heroes.

rod_of_atos.coaching_tip: Long-range initiation tool to lock enemies in place for follow-up spells. Root prevents movement, blink, and TP, but does not prevent attacking or casting. Great on heroes with skillshot stuns.

orchid.coaching_tip: Rush it against spell-dependent heroes like Storm Spirit, Puck, Anti-Mage, or Ember Spirit. The 30% damage amp at the end is significant burst. Upgrade to Bloodthorn for even more damage.

counter_tips.Storm Spirit: Orchid Malevolence silences Storm Spirit and prevents Ball Lightning, effectively rooting one of the most mobile heroes in the game. The damage amplification from Soul Burn can burst Storm before the silence ends. Storm must buy Eul's Scepter or BKB to counter Orchid, delaying his damage items significantly.
counter_tips.Queen of Pain: Orchid Malevolence silences Queen of Pain's Blink, preventing her escape and keeping her in place for your team. Soul Burn's damage amplification makes QoP's low HP pool even more fragile. QoP must rush Eul's or BKB to counter Orchid, disrupting her preferred item build.
counter_tips.Puck: Orchid Malevolence prevents Phase Shift, Illusory Orb, and all of Puck's escape tools. Puck is extremely fragile when silenced and the Soul Burn damage amplification ensures a quick kill. Puck must buy Eul's Scepter or Linken's Sphere to survive Orchid, delaying Blink Dagger timing.

shivas_guard.coaching_tip: Excellent against physical attack-speed-based lineups. The attack speed reduction aura is constant and passive. Use the active blast at the start of teamfights for the AoE slow.

manta.coaching_tip: The basic dispel on activation removes silences, slows, and many debuffs. Use it reactively to dispel, not just to push lanes. Agi carry core item for the dispel, illusions, and stats.

ethereal_blade.coaching_tip: Combo tool for magic burst heroes -- cast it, then follow up with nukes while the target takes 30% more magic damage. Can also self-cast defensively against physical attackers. Morphling uses it offensively with Adaptive Strike.

aether_lens.coaching_tip: Increases your initiation range, making it easier to land spells from a safe distance. Core on supports who need to stay at the back of fights.

wind_waker.coaching_tip: Upgraded Eul's that can save allies. Use it on teammates to buy time or dispel debuffs. The ability to cyclone allies makes it one of the best late-game support items.

gungir.coaching_tip: An AoE root for initiation and catch: rooted heroes cannot walk or blink out. Wait until enemies are clumped, the radius is only 400. Since 7.38 it has no chain lightning any more, so buy it for the root and the area-of-effect bonus, not to farm.

ancient_janggo.coaching_tip: Cost-effective mid-game aura item for push-oriented lineups. Use the active during pushes and teamfights. Great early team item, but sell it later when inventory space is needed.

holy_locket.coaching_tip: Core for healing-oriented supports like Dazzle, Chen, Warlock, Omniknight, and Oracle. The passive amplifies every heal you provide by 10%, and the active adds 15% incoming heal amplification on one ally for 4s on top of the charge heal: use it on the hero your team is trying to keep alive.

veil_of_discord.coaching_tip: Use it on grouped enemies before your team unleashes magic damage. Great in magic-heavy lineups. Apply it at the start of fights to amplify all your team's magical burst.

abyssal_blade.coaching_tip: The active stun pierces BKB, making it the go-to lockdown for carries against BKB carriers. Use the active stun on priority targets who have already used BKB. Blink + Abyssal is a reliable kill combo.

bfury.coaching_tip: A farming accelerator -- buy it early to speed up your farm. The cleave lets you clear jungle camps and creep waves rapidly. Best on heroes who can fight with it later (PA crits cleave, Ember Sleight).

armlet.coaching_tip: Master the Armlet toggle technique -- at low health, quickly toggling it off and on gives you back the health of its +25 Strength, and the toggle itself cannot kill you. Toggle it on before fights and off between fights. Huskar's passive synergizes perfectly with the HP drain.

echo_sabre.coaching_tip: The double attack is excellent for burst damage and applying on-hit effects twice. Great on Slark for double Essence Shift stacks. Builds into Harpoon later.

hand_of_midas.coaching_tip: Buy it early or not at all -- it needs time to pay off. Transmute pays 160 gold whatever the target and no longer gives bonus experience; a neutral creep also drops a madstone bundle, so use it in the jungle whenever it is ready (it cannot target Ancients). Do not skip it just because you had a good lane; it ensures late-game scaling.

blade_mail.coaching_tip: Force enemies to choose: attack you and take damage back, or switch targets. Best on initiators who jump into the enemy team (Axe, Legion Commander, Centaur). Activate it right as you engage.

dagon.coaching_tip: Burst magic damage for pickoffs and snowballing. Most effective in the early-mid game when enemy HP pools are small. Falls off hard in late game. Combine with Ethereal Blade for maximum burst damage.

maelstrom.coaching_tip: A mid-game farming item and teamfight damage multiplier. Works on ranged and melee heroes alike. Builds into Mjollnir. Great for heroes who need AoE damage to farm faster.

angels_demise.coaching_tip: A Phylactery upgrade: your next unit-target spell on an enemy deals 250 extra damage, disables the target's passives (Break) and slows it by 30% for 4 seconds. Its value is the Break: buy it on a hero with a cheap unit-target spell when the enemy relies on passives, like Bristleback or Phantom Assassin.

disperser.coaching_tip: Upgraded Diffusal Blade with a powerful dispel. Self-cast to dispel debuffs and gain max move speed for chasing or escaping. Cast on enemies for a crippling slow. Extremely versatile.

harpoon.coaching_tip: Gap-closer for melee carries who struggle to get on top of targets. Use it to catch fleeing heroes or close the distance to start fighting. Builds from Echo Sabre.

devastator.coaching_tip: Powerful on Int heroes who auto-attack frequently. The spell debuff amplifies follow-up magic damage, making it excellent for heroes who chain spells and right-clicks together.

basher.coaching_tip: Locks down targets with repeated stuns. Best on fast-attacking melee heroes who proc the bash often. Upgrade to Abyssal Blade for the guaranteed BKB-piercing active stun.

mage_slayer.coaching_tip: Hard counter to spell-dependent cores. Attack the enemy caster to reduce their spell damage output by 40%. Particularly effective on illusion heroes since illusions also apply the debuff.

bloodstone.coaching_tip: Core on spell casters who deal sustained damage. Press Bloodpact right as your damage starts: for 5 seconds 60% of the spell damage you deal comes back as health, which is what keeps Storm Spirit or Leshrac alive inside a fight. The aura does not stack with Veil of Discord.

hurricane_pike.coaching_tip: Upgraded Force Staff for ranged carries and supports. The active pushes you and the enemy apart and lets you make 5 attacks on that target without range limit within 5 seconds -- perfect for kiting melee heroes. Also works as an escape tool.

solar_crest.coaching_tip: A buff for one ally, not for yourself: Shine gives the target 5 armor, 60 attack speed, 15% movement speed and a 350 physical damage barrier for 7 seconds. Cast it on your carry as the fight starts; it cannot be cast on enemies. One of the most cost-effective items for supports.

meteor_hammer.coaching_tip: The channeling time requires a setup stun or from fog of war. Can hit buildings, making it useful for split-pushing. Chain it off reliable disables for guaranteed damage and stun.

octarine_core.coaching_tip: The 25% cooldown reduction affects everything -- abilities, items, and even BKB. Best on heroes who spam abilities frequently. The CDR on items like Blink Dagger and BKB is especially valuable.

moon_shard.coaching_tip: Consume it when you are six-slotted for a permanent 60 attack speed bonus that does not take an inventory slot. Buy it for the 140 attack speed boost when you need raw DPS in the late game.

vladmir.coaching_tip: An efficient team aura item that benefits all allies. The percentage-based damage and lifesteal scale well into the late game. Great on melee offlaners or supports who stay near the team.

helm_of_the_overlord.coaching_tip: Dominate an Ancient creep for powerful auras or abilities (e.g., Thunderhide for attack speed aura, Granite Golem for HP aura). The dominated creep can push lanes and scout. Micro-intensive but extremely rewarding.

boots_of_bearing.coaching_tip: Upgraded Drum of Endurance with a more powerful active. The undispellable initial burst of speed allows your team to engage or disengage even against slows. Great for push-oriented and teamfight-centric strategies.

witch_blade.coaching_tip: Cost-effective damage item for Int heroes who right-click often. The slow and bonus damage proc helps with laning and pickoffs. Falls off late game, so consider upgrading or selling.

phylactery.coaching_tip: Budget burst damage amplifier for spell-focused heroes. The 150 bonus damage procs reliably with low-cooldown spells. Excellent mid-game pickup for supports who need more damage output.

kaya_and_sange.coaching_tip: Best on spell-casting cores who also need survivability. The slow resistance keeps you moving through slows and the health restoration bonus strengthens your healing and lifesteal, while the spell amplification boosts your damage. Ideal for front-line casters.

sange_and_yasha.coaching_tip: A well-rounded fighting item for melee carries. The status resistance means stuns and slows last shorter on you, which is crucial for heroes who need to stay on targets. Good mid-game timing item.

yasha_and_kaya.coaching_tip: Ideal for mobile, spell-heavy cores who also benefit from attack speed. The move speed and spell amp combination suits heroes who weave in and out of fights, like Storm Spirit or Ember Spirit.

arcane_blink.coaching_tip: The longest Blink (1400 range) and the only one that restores resources: 250 health and 100 mana on arrival. Take it on casters who initiate from far away and need the mana for the combo that follows.

overwhelming_blink.coaching_tip: Adds AoE damage and slow on your Blink initiation. Best on strength initiators who jump into the enemy team. The slow gives your team time to follow up on your initiation.

swift_blink.coaching_tip: The agility hero's Blink upgrade. After blinking you gain 40% phased movement speed and +35 Agility for 6 seconds, which is ideal for carries who blink in to burst a target. Excellent on heroes who already use Blink offensively.

consecrated_wraps.coaching_tip: A shield that recharges by itself: with 3 charges the first hit of a fight lands on a 360 barrier. A new charge only comes every 4s and all of them are spent at once, so it is strongest against poke and the opening burst and adds little in a long brawl. There is nothing to press.

crellas_crozier.coaching_tip: A Ghost Scepter upgrade with an anti-heal aura. Use the active when physical damage is on you, but like Ghost Scepter it makes magic damage hurt more, and it does nothing while you are debuff immune. It shares its cooldown with Ghost Scepter. Standing in the fight is enough for the aura to cut the enemy's healing.

essence_distiller.coaching_tip: An Urn of Shadows upgrade. Besides the heal and the damage, the enemy cast gives True Sight and the target's vision for 8 seconds: use it on heroes who go invisible or run into fog. Ground-cast it on a choke point to tag whoever walks in.

specialists_array.coaching_tip: Only ranged heroes get the Splitshot. It speeds up farming and wave clear for ranged carries and builds into Hydra's Breath; the extra projectiles carry no on-hit effects, so it adds little against a single target.

hydras_breath.coaching_tip: A late-game item for ranged right-clickers: the max-HP poison is damage against high-health heroes and the multi-shot spreads it across a fight. Its attack range does not stack with Dragon Lance, Hurricane Pike or Monkey King Bar.
